A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same BioProAgent study, with matching core sections, experiments, and figures. v1 ends after the references despite citing appendices; v2 supplies Appendices A-I. Newly documented material can be distinguished from retained content.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.6 report original BioProBench simulation results, including benchmark comparisons, error correction, execution traces, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional Oracle-ReAct, error-type, and thinking-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The overall FSM, memory, and hierarchical verification architecture remains. The stated planner projection changes from symbolic keys alone to keys with semantic previews (Equation 2), and Equation 3 replaces the APPROVED-state execution condition with a verified-code condition.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four extended BioProBench subsets and 22-device environment. Appendix F newly documents dataset composition and sample counts. Oracle-ReAct and thinking-model experiments use retained Subsets C/D; additional domains or task coverage are not established.

E2.justification: Section 4.2.4 adds Oracle-ReAct with forced verification, and Table 17 adds direct DeepSeek-V3.2-Think and Gemini-3-Pro-Think comparisons on Subsets C/D. These substantially strengthen the alternatives tested. Qwen and Kimi gain Table 3 rows but already appeared in v1's Figure 1.

E3.justification: Table 4 replaces Subset D sequence accuracy with correction success, explicitly defined as Cp > 0.8. Added experiments introduce forced-PASS termination for Oracle-ReAct and direct-versus-agent configurations for thinking models. Other newly supplied settings document existing experiments without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether mandatory verification rescues ReAct and whether stronger reasoning models replace or improve the framework. Appendix F.2 adds quantitative error-type breakdowns. Existing component ablations remain, with materially revised Subset D outcomes and explanations.

E5.justification: Both already report paired t-tests and cross-judge Pearson correlations. Tables 11 and 13 supply more detailed outcomes under those practices. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Subset D Cp changes from 0.887 to 0.925. Table 6 changes w/o FSM from 0.000 to 0.782 and w/o Verification from 0.870 to 0.782. Added results include detailed judge/error breakdowns and Table 17's strong direct-model performance and agent-backbone failures. The new 90.0% correction success is a different metric from v1's 0.464 sequence accuracy.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces the five-bit signal space with mixed Boolean/ternary signals and revises formal grounding and execution definitions. Appendix E supplies custom score definitions, while Appendix F.1 adds a compounding-error calculation. The conditional safety assumptions remain, without a new safety proof.

C1.justification: The introduction revises advertised error-recovery success from 88.7% to 90.0%, alongside the newly explicit success definition. The training-free FSM and grounding contributions, abstract's 95.6% compliance claim, and conclusion about the necessity of symbolic safety interlocks remain.

C2.justification: Appendix G introduces reasoning-context overflow as a limitation of thinking-model backbones and emphasizes efficiency with lightweight models. Section 4.6 interprets the revised 0.782 ablation score as unchanged corrupted-input compliance. Appendix F adds trajectory-complexity arguments and repair limitations; the original simulation and hardware-registration limitations remain.

D1.justification: Previously absent appendices now provide tool signatures, expanded FSM rules, representative hardware schemas, metric weights and thresholds, benchmark composition, and planner, alignment, and baseline prompts. These substantially improve implementation and evaluation documentation. Existing code and project links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds physics-aware rejection sampling through Hyun et al. New appendix citations include KeyBERT and Gemini 3 Pro. The broader research positioning remains; updates to SciAgents and other existing references principally correct bibliographic information.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most narrative remain. Localized rewrites expand memory/control explanations and revise error-correction and ablation passages. Grammar, affiliations, acknowledgments, and cross-references change, while the new appendices organize supporting material.

P2.justification: v2 adds extensive appendix tables covering specifications, statistical checks, task complexity, error breakdowns, model scaling, and execution logs, plus boxed prompt listings. Table 3 expands and Table 4 changes its correction metric column. Existing figures are largely retained, with some displays relocated or elaborated.

improvement.justification: v1 directs readers to absent appendices for essential specifications and validation. v2 supplies much of that material and adds challenging controls that expose important strengths and failures, substantially improving reproducibility and assessability. Important issues remain: Appendix E.3 requires Cp = 1 for success, whereas Table 4 reports 100% success with Cp = 0.950, and Table 17's strong direct-model results qualify the retained necessity claims.
